title: fix: parse chat content arrays in Play
author: Circuit-Overtime
pr_body_excerpt:
- Extracts text from OpenAI content-parts arrays before rendering chat results.
- Keeps existing string-content behavior unchanged.
- Supports Floret responses containing text plus linked media parts.

Split from #14294.

gist.headline: Play reads the whole bouquet
gist.blurb: Chat replies in Play can now unpack OpenAI-style content parts before putting words on screen. Floret may bring text and media together; the UI now knows where the text lives.
gist.summary: PlayGenerator now extracts text from OpenAI content-part arrays, so Floret chat responses that combine text with linked media render their written result while existing string responses continue unchanged.
gist.impact: Users can see the text in mixed Floret text-and-media responses in Play instead of receiving a chat result the renderer cannot read.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli as a cheerful little librarian or gardener sorting a bouquet of message cards: readable text cards and tiny linked image/media cards from a Floret chat response. A retro Play terminal displays the extracted text clearly, with code-plants and flowers around it to show that the mixed response has been carefully parsed rather than discarded.
gist.image_prompt: Cozy pixel art scene of Polli, the cute yellow-and-brown striped bee mascot with pink blush, light blue wings, and tiny librarian glasses, sorting a Floret chat bouquet of text cards and linked media tiles beside a glowing retro monitor that cleanly displays the extracted message. Lime green (#ecf874) is prominent across the terminal glow and flower pots, with code-plants, soft mint-lavender-peach gradients, cozy pixel art, 8-bit aesthetic, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes, and subtle pixel-font text: 'PLAY'.
